# Statistics Exam Prep Plan for Berlin Student

A focused 18-day revision plan built around **90 minutes on weekdays** and **3 hours on weekends**, with extra attention on **hypothesis testing** and **regression**. The schedule uses spaced repetition so core formulas and methods stay fresh through exam day on **2026-06-12**.

# 18-Day Revision Schedule

| Day | Time | Focus | Key Tasks | Goal |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | 90 min | Setup + diagnostics | Gather notes; list topics; do a 20-minute mini quiz; mark weak areas | Clear study map |
| Day 2 | 90 min | Descriptive stats | Mean, median, variance, SD; interpret outputs | Fast recall of basics |
| Day 3 | 90 min | Probability review | Rules, conditional probability, distributions | Build foundation |
| Day 4 | 90 min | Hypothesis testing I | Null/alternative, p-values, errors, one-sample tests | Understand test logic |
| Day 5 | 90 min | Hypothesis testing II | Two-sample tests, paired tests, choosing the right test | Identify test types |
| Day 6 | 3 hours | Hypothesis testing practice | Work mixed problems; correct mistakes; make a formula sheet | Stronger test accuracy |
| Day 7 | 3 hours | Regression I | Correlation, simple linear regression, interpretation | Read regression output |
| Day 8 | 90 min | Regression II | Assumptions, residuals, R², slope meaning | Spot model issues |
| Day 9 | 90 min | Spaced review 1 | Revisit Days 2–5; flashcards; 15-minute recall drill | Lock in earlier topics |
| Day 10 | 90 min | Confidence intervals | Construct, interpret, compare to hypothesis tests | Connect concepts |
| Day 11 | 90 min | Regression practice | Solve 4–6 problems; interpret coefficients and plots | Speed + accuracy |
| Day 12 | 3 hours | Timed mixed set 1 | 60–75 min timed practice; review every error | Simulate exam pressure |
| Day 13 | 90 min | Spaced review 2 | Rework missed questions; refine formula sheet | Fix weak spots |
| Day 14 | 90 min | Probability + distributions | Normal, t, chi-square basics; when to use each | Improve test selection |
| Day 15 | 3 hours | Full practice test | Take one full mock under exam conditions; then review | Final readiness check |
| Day 16 | 90 min | Error correction | Re-do missed mock questions; focus on weak patterns | Convert mistakes into points |
| Day 17 | 90 min | Final spaced review | Flashcards; formulas; hypothesis testing and regression summary | Fresh recall |
| Day 18 | 60–90 min | Light pre-exam review | Quick formula pass; 2 easy problems; stop early | Stay calm and sharp |

# Spaced Repetition and Practice Test Timing

## Review rhythm
- **Same day:** 5-minute recap right after each session.
- **Next day:** 10-minute recall of yesterday’s key ideas.
- **3 days later:** Short mixed practice on the same topic.
- **7 days later:** Re-test with a few harder questions.
- **Final 48 hours:** Only light review, no heavy new material.

## What to repeat most often
- **Hypothesis testing:** null/alternative, p-values, Type I/II errors, test selection.
- **Regression:** slope meaning, R², residuals, assumptions, interpreting output.
- **Formula sheet:** update it every 2–3 days, then use it for active recall only.

## Practice test timing
- **Day 12:** Timed mixed set, about **60–75 minutes**, then review.
- **Day 15:** Full mock exam in one sitting, matching exam timing as closely as possible.
- **Day 16:** Redo only the questions missed on the mock, without notes first.

# Day-By-Day Focus Notes

## Days 1–6: Build the core
- Start with a diagnostic so you do not waste time on topics you already know.
- Put the most time into **hypothesis testing**, since that is a weak area.
- On weekend Day 6, spend the last 30 minutes making a one-page “must-know” sheet.

## Days 7–12: Strengthen regression and mixed problem-solving
- Learn regression in layers: interpretation first, then assumptions, then calculation.
- Use mixed sets to practice choosing between tests and methods.
- Keep an error log with 3 columns: topic, mistake, correct rule.

## Days 13–18: Consolidate and taper
- Focus on recall, not reading.
- If a problem takes too long, mark it and move on.
- Reduce workload on the final day so you arrive rested.

# Exam Day Checklist

- Bring **student ID**, pens/pencils, calculator, and any allowed formula sheet.
- Sleep 7–8 hours the night before.
- Eat a normal breakfast with protein and water.
- Arrive early and use the first minutes to skim formulas.
- Start with the questions you know best to build confidence.
- Watch for common traps: wrong test choice, sign errors, and misreading regression output.
- Leave 5–10 minutes at the end to check calculations and units.
